CONFIRM C0006 | The fix correctly returns 1.0 when cum_r <= cum_1, which properly handles the case where cross-round clustering reduces the total number of equivalence classes (a strong signal of convergence).
CHALLENGE C0004 | `novel_sev` can never exceed `total_sev`. Any novel class in round `r` must be disconnected from all prior findings (otherwise it is not novel). Therefore, novel classes in round `r` will form isolated components in the cumulative graph, meaning their exact aggregated severities will be added to `total_sev`. Thus `novel_sev <= total_sev` is a mathematical guarantee under single-linkage clustering.
CHALLENGE C0014 | Under single-linkage clustering, if any member of a class is similar to a prior finding, the entire class will merge into the prior cumulative cluster. Therefore, no member of that class represents a genuinely new, disconnected cluster. Excluding the entire class is mathematically correct and consistent with the definition of novelty in a single-linkage graph.
